text.p: A five-nation monitoring group that includes the United States on Wednesday held Israel responsible for shelling a south Lebanon village and "deplored" the injury it caused to a civilian woman.

"Israeli forces were responsible for the manner in which they carried out their mortar fire which resulted in the injury and damage at Louwaizeh," UNIFIL, the U.N. peacekeeping force in south Lebanon, said in a statement on the monitors' meeting.

The statement followed a two-day meeting by representatives of the United States, France, Lebanon, Syria and Israel at UNIFIL headquarters in the coastal village of Naqoura in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, called to discuss a complaint lodged by Beirut over the incident.

It was the second time the committee has blamed Israel for shelling a south Lebanon village since the monitoring group was formed under a U.S.-brokered ceasefire that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon in April.
Lebanon had complained that Israeli shelling of Louwaizeh on Sunday wounded a woman and damaged three houses, a mosque, a cemetery and a vehicle.
The Israeli bombardment followed an attack by pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas that killed an Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army (SLA) militiaman.

"The monitoring group deplored the injury caused to the Lebanese civilian," the statement said, adding the committee believed Israeli forces "might have taken more effective precautions to avoid such consequences".
On October 18 the group had "deplored" an Israeli bombardment that injured 13 civilians in Safad al-Batikh and urged measures to prevent any repetition.
In Beirut, Foreign Minister Faris Bouez played down the decision: "No one expected from the start that the committee would be able to deter Israel aggressions."

The group was set up to monitor breaches of the ceasefire that ended an Israeli pounding of Lebanon in April in which 200 people, mostly civilians, were killed. The blitz was aimed at ending Hizbollah rocket attacks on northern Israel.
The agreement bars Hizbollah and Israel from firing from or at civilian targets but allows raids on Israeli troops occupying south Lebanon and gives both sides the right to self-defence.
The monitors failed to reach agreement on a second complaint by Beirut over what it said was the expulsion of two Lebanese families from the Israeli-held south Lebanon zone.
"They noted a proposal by one of the delegations to raise the matter in diplomatic channels on a bilateral basis with a view to reaching a satisfactory solution," the statement said.
